newsitem.title: GERMANY: Tietmeyer says EMU criteria must be met honestly.
newsitem.headline: Tietmeyer says EMU criteria must be met honestly.

text.p: Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer on Tuesday warned nations against tailoring their finances in order to pass the entry test to Europe's currency union, saying such moves would undermine the new currency.

"I view certain beauty operations with worry as they are clearly designed to improve the finances for the appointed date," Tietmeyer said in a speech prepared for delivery to a group of foreign bankers.
"One-time efforts are not appropriate to create the necessary trust in the Euro."
In a bid to be among the first group of nations to join the European currency union in 1999, several nations are using special one-off factors to adjust their finances.
France, for example, will be able to use funds from a transfer from France Telecom to reduce its budget deficit in 1997.
Tietmeyer warned confidence and trust in the new currency could be created only if the right nations enter the union.
"It is absolutely necessary that only nations with a convergent stability policy and sufficiently solid public finances can enter the currency union."
"A beautifully posed photograph on a sunny day does not set the stage for a good future," Tietmeyer said.

Tietmeyer, known as one of the staunchest supporters for a strict interpretation of the Maastricht Treaty criteria, also said "in the interest of a stable currency union, all criteria must be fulfilled."

There has been growing talk that nations may not need to meet all the criteria on stable currencies, low inflation and interest rates and low deficit and debt ratios to overall gross domestic product.
